title: The Credential and the Skill
sentences: Education has quietly split into two enterprises that share a building.
One teaches; the other certifies, and only the second is priced.
Employers rarely inspect what was learned, since inspection is expensive.
They read the certificate instead, which is cheap and roughly indicative.
This arrangement holds only while the two remain loosely correlated.
Every incentive in the system works to loosen that correlation further.
Students optimise for the signal, as any rational person would.
Institutions, competing for those students, learn to supply it generously.
The result is not fraud so much as a slow drift of purpose.
What is finally sold is admission to a category rather than a competence.
